title: Credential mesh + KMS-proxy upgrade notes (v0.1, draft)
body:
Summary:

This is a working draft for migrating private deployments from our current Vault-centric secrets proxy to a lightweight "credential mesh" backed by a KMS-proxy and HSM-backed root keys. Goal: reduce operational surface for customers, eliminate long-lived symmetric key import/replication across on-prem clusters, and provide stronger tamper-evident audit trails while preserving offline/air-gapped installability.

High-level goals:
- Replace current Vault remote-secret flow with per-cluster short-lived wrapping keys issued by a central KMS hierarchy (HSM root).
- Provide a KMS-proxy service that runs inside customer VPCs/on-prem control planes; proxy authenticates to local HSM or remote KMS depending on environment.
- Make Terraform modules minimal-change for customers: new resources are optional feature flags; migration has clear import paths.
- Ensure audit logs are consistent, tamper-evident, and ship to customer audit sinks with signed envelopes.

Background and motivation:
- Current pattern (vault-as-a-service + replicated sealed secrets) has worked but: operational complexity for customers, key copy proliferation, and audit gaps for HSM-backed key operations.
- We want: HSM-backed root key (Redwood-managed for Hosted, customer-managed HSM for Private), ephemeral per-cluster wrapping keys, KV-cache invalidation on rotation, and structured audit events.

Design overview (credential mesh):
- Root: HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Azure HSM / customer HSM appliance). Root key never leaves HSM; it signs key-issue operations and attestation statements.
- KMS-proxy: lightweight daemon that runs in-cluster (or in customer control plane). Responsibilities:
  - Authenticate service identity (mTLS + SPIFFE or existing bootstrap tokens).
  - Request wrapping keys (short TTL) from Redwood control plane or local HSM via a defined API.
  - Perform envelope encryption/decryption for secrets at rest and produce signed audit envelopes.
- Per-cluster wrapping keys: asymmetric or symmetric depending on HSM capabilities. Default: AES-GCM wrapping with ephemeral key derived from HSM-signed CSR. TTL default 24h.
- Caching: prefix/KV caches still allowed; cache invalidation hook tied to key rotation events (pubsub/route).

HSM/KMS integration patterns (supported):
- Hosted Redwood: Redwood HSM (CloudHSM) signs key issue JWTs; KMS-proxy uses REST to retrieve wrapping keys encrypted under the HSM root.
- Dedicated: Customer can bring HSM into our dedicated VPC peering arrangement; we provide a connector to sign CSR and return wrapped keys.
- On-prem/air-gapped: KMS-proxy runs entirely local and uses a hardware HSM appliance (Thales/Luna) accessible via PKCS#11. Root key imported via an offline ceremony (see migration steps).

Terraform module notes (what to add/change):
- New module: modules/kms-proxy (optional). Exported inputs:
  - enabled (bool)
  - mode: hosted | customer-hsm | onprem
  - hsm_config_id (optional, only for customer-hsm/onprem)
  - audit_forwarder_endpoint
  - service_identity_sa / spiffe / bootstrap_token
- Outputs:
  - kms_proxy_endpoint
  - kms_proxy_cert_thumbprint
  - rotation_schedule_id
- Resource-level guidance:
  - Introduce aws_kms_alias-like abstraction only for hosted mode; do NOT create keys by default for onprem.
  - Add data source: redwood_hsm_root_info to detect existing root and avoid duplicate imports.
  - Provide import scripts: terraform import redwood_kms_proxy.<name> <existing-resource-id>
- Backwards compatibility:
  - Default behavior: if module not present, fallback to legacy vault-proxy behavior (no forced rotate).
  - Module flag "migrate_vault_secrets" will run post-apply helper to rewrap secrets from Vault ciphertext to credential-mesh envelopes. This helper is an out-of-band script (see linked PR).

Upgrade & migration plan (phased):
Phase 0: Pre-checks (days -7 to -3)
- Inventory all clusters with vault-proxy enabled (query CMDB + terraform state).
- Confirm customer HSM availability / offline ceremony windows with security contact.
- Create per-customer migration ticket and schedule.

Phase 1: Staging canary (day 0)
- Deploy kms-proxy module into a staging cluster. Mode = hosted (Redwood HSM) to validate flows.
- Smoke tests: encrypt/decrypt roundtrip, TTL rotation, audit envelope creation, and log forwarder.
- Validate Terraform import path: import existing vault-proxy resources into new module state.

Phase 2: Controlled migration (day 1-7)
- For each customer cluster (start with low-risk): enable kms-proxy in read-only mode (decrypt only) for a 24-48h shadow period.
- Run rewrap helper to re-encrypt secrets into credential-mesh envelopes in a staging store.
- Run 72h canary traffic with dual-read and compare outputs (checksum + semantic tests).

Phase 3: Cutover and rotate (day 8-14)
- Schedule 1-hour maintenance window per cluster: flip primary secret provider to credential-mesh, rotate wrapping keys, purge old vault cache.
- Post-cutover tests, escalate on failure to rollback plan.

Phase 4: Post-mig & audit (day 15-30)
- Retain legacy Vault read-only for 30 days for drift checks.
- Verify audit trails: signed envelopes present, log forwarding healthy, and audits match expected key events.

Rollback plan:
- Before cutover: can disable module and keep Vault proxy as primary.
- During cutover: if decryption errors exceed threshold (5% of requests or 100 errors) -> revert DNS/service routing to Vault-proxy and re-issue rollback runbook (fast path uses cached old wrapping keys).
- After cutover: full restore requires re-importing Vault ciphertexts if credential-mesh cannot decrypt; helper script preserves original Vault ciphertexts until TTL expiry.

Security & audit log schema:
- Event format (JSON): {"ts","cluster","actor","op","key_id","envelope_signature","hsm_cert_serial","outcome","trace_id","redwood_ticket"} (we will publish a JSON schema in Confluence).
- Signed envelopes: every KMS-proxy response includes a base64 signature from HSM root key attesting to the operation and a nonce. This allows offline verification if audit logs are transported.
- Log forwarding: KMS-proxy ships events to configured forwarders (syslog / s3-compatible / splunk). For air-gapped installs, provide a signed batch file for customer SIEM pickup.

Observability & SLOs:
- Metrics to emit:
  - kms_proxy.requests_total, kms_proxy.decrypt_errors, kms_proxy.rotate_success_total, kms_proxy.cache_miss_total
- SLO targets: 99.9% decrypt success within 50ms for local-proxy mode; for hosted fetches allow 200ms tail.
- Alerts: >1% error rate sustained for 5m, rotation failures, audit forwarder lag >10m.

Testing & validation (what to automate):
- Unit: encryption/decryption code paths (including PKCS#11 and AWS HSM mocks).
- Integration: end-to-end test in ephemeral cluster with local HSM emulator (SoftHSM) + terraform apply + rewrap helper.
- Chaos: simulate HSM unreachable, network partitions, and key rotation during heavy traffic.
- Regression: prompt-level semantic validation for LLM models that depend on secrets (e.g., license retrieval flows).

Operational runbooks (short checklist):
- Pre-cutover checklist (ops owner, 24h): verify backups, export Vault ciphertext archive, verify auth tokens, schedule maintenance window with customer.
- Cutover checklist (ops owner, 1h window): enable kms-proxy, flush caches, rotate wrapping key, run smoke tests, confirm audit envelope signatures present.
- Post-cutover (ops owner, 72h): monitor error rates, validate forwarding, run drift detection script.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Key type: do we use asymmetric wraps by default? Asymmetric wrapping simplifies import but increases HSM op size. (ACTION: decision needed from crypto team - ENGSEC-742).
- Customer HSM integration surface: what minimum PKCS#11 subset do we require for appliance vendors? (ACTION: list vendor matrix).
- Offline key ceremony cadence: recommend quarterly ceremonies, need legal/compliance sign-off for some regions.

Next steps / owners:
- Marcus: prototype kms-proxy daemon (PoC) and push initial docker image. (ETA: 2024-12-13) [GH PR linked above]
- Leila: Terraform module skeleton and import scripts (ETA: 2024-12-18).
- Tomás: Draft audit JSON schema and forwarder adapters (ETA: 2024-12-09).
- Asha: coordinate customer pilot schedule and runbooks (ETA: 2024-12-06).

Work items / TODOs (quick list):
- [ ] Write Confluence page with final JSON schema and migration checklist (owner: Tomás).
- [ ] Add terraform import helper and examples to infra repo under docs/kms-migration (owner: Leila).
- [ ] Build SoftHSM-based test harness and add to CI for nightly integration (owner: Marcus).
- [ ] Create customer-facing migration one-pager summarizing impact and downtime windows (owner: Asha).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Keep legacy Vault read-only for at least 30 days; always preserve original ciphertexts as an escape hatch.
- Consider a "sign-only" HSM mode for customers who cannot export keys but can accept signed attestations. This reduces key movement risk.

References and helpful links:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1289
- Jira epic: ENGSEC-742 (KMS/HSM integration roadmap)
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/987654321/Private+Deployments+KMS+Strategy

Feedback welcome — this is intentionally rough. I expect we will iterate on the key type decision and the import scripts before locking the terraform module interface.
